text:
The Specific Relief Act, 1963
Part II: Specific Relief and Recovery of Possession
Section 6: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property

Statutory Text:
If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person through whom he has been in possession or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof, notwithstanding any other title that may be set up in such suit. No suit under this section shall be brought: (a) after the expiry of six months from the date of dispossession; or (b) against the Government.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: File summary suit within 6 months to instantly recover physical possession without proving title.

text:
The Specific Relief Act, 1963
Part II: Specific Relief and Recovery of Possession
Section 10: Specific performance in respect of contracts

Statutory Text:
The specific performance of a contract shall be enforced by the court subject to the provisions contained in sub-section (2) of section 11, section 14 and section 16. Specific performance is now a mandatory statutory right rather than an equitable discretion.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Court compels the defaulting party to execute sale deed or perform specific contractual duties.

text:
The Specific Relief Act, 1963
Part II: Specific Relief and Recovery of Possession
Section 38: Perpetual injunction when granted

Statutory Text:
Subject to the other provisions contained in or referred to by this Chapter, a perpetual injunction may be granted to the plaintiff to prevent the breach of an obligation existing in his favour, whether expressly or by implication. When the defendant invades or threatens to invade the plaintiff's right to, or enjoyment of, property.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Obtain permanent stay order / injunction against property encroachment or harassment.

The Limitation Act, 1963
Part II & Schedule: Limitation of Suits, Appeals and Applications
Section 3: Bar of limitation

Statutory Text:
Subject to the provisions contained in sections 4 to 24 (inclusive), every suit instituted, appeal preferred, and application made after the prescribed period shall be dismissed, although limitation has not been set up as a defence.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Legal suits must strictly be instituted within statutory limitation periods.

text:
The Limitation Act, 1963
Part II & Schedule: Limitation of Suits, Appeals and Applications
Article 7 & 113: Limitation period for recovery of wages and general money claims (3 Years)

Statutory Text:
The period of limitation for a suit for wages in the case of any other person not otherwise specifically provided for is three years from the date when the wages accrue due. For any suit for which no period of limitation is provided elsewhere in the Schedule, the period is three years from when the right to sue accrues.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Civil suits for recovery of unpaid salary or debt must be filed within 3 years from due date.

text:
The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
Chapter IV & VI: Criteria for Giving Legal Services and Lok Adalats
Section 12: Criteria for giving free legal services / Free Legal Aid

Statutory Text:
Every person who has to file or defend a case shall be entitled to legal services under this Act if that person, is: (a) a member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe; (b) a victim of trafficking in human beings or beggar; (c) a woman or a child; (d) a person with disability; (e) an industrial workman; (f) a person in custody; (g) a person with annual income less than prescribed ceiling (₹3,00,000 in Delhi/States). Free legal aid includes payment of court fees, drafting charges, advocate fees, and process expenses.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Eligible citizens receive 100% free advocate appointment, court fee payment, and drafting support.

The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
Chapter IV & VI: Criteria for Giving Legal Services and Lok Adalats
Section 19 & 21: Organization of Lok Adalats and Finality of Award

Statutory Text:
Every award of the Lok Adalat shall be deemed to be a decree of a civil court and no appeal shall lie to any court against the award of the Lok Adalat. Lok Adalats facilitate fast, binding, amicable settlements without court fee.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Lok Adalat awards are final, non-appealable, and trigger 100% refund of court fees already deposited.

text:
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
Chapter I: Preliminary Definitions
Section 2(7): Definition of Consumer

Statutory Text:
Consumer means any person who: (i) buys any goods for a consideration which has been paid or promised or partly paid and partly promised; (ii) hires or avails of any service for a consideration. It includes offline and online transactions through electronic means or teleshopping or direct selling. Does not include a person who obtains goods for commercial resale purposes.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Qualifies all individual buyers (online and offline) for consumer dispute protection.

text:
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
Chapter I: Preliminary Definitions
Section 2(11): Deficiency in Service

Statutory Text:
Deficiency means any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature and manner of performance which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or has been undertaken to be performed by a person in pursuance of a contract or otherwise in relation to any service. Includes: (i) any act of negligence or omission or commission by such person which causes loss or injury to the consumer; and (ii) deliberate withholding of relevant information by such person to the consumer.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Right to claim replacement, refund, and compensation for deficiency in service.

text:
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
Chapter I: Preliminary Definitions
Section 2(47): Unfair Trade Practice and Counterfeit / Fake Goods

Statutory Text:
Unfair trade practice means a trade practice which, for the purpose of promoting the sale, use or supply of any goods or for the provision of any service, adopts any unfair method or deceptive practice. Includes: (i) falsely representing goods/services of particular standard/quality or brand; (ii) false warranty or guarantee; (iii) refusing to refund or replace defective or counterfeit goods within promised timeline; (iv) selling duplicate/fake products or disclosing consumer personal information without consent.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Prohibits deceptive trade practices and empowers commissions to award punitive damages and full refund.

text:
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
Chapter IV: Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Section 34: Jurisdiction of District Commission

Statutory Text:
Subject to the other provisions of this Act, the District Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration does not exceed fifty lakh rupees. A complaint may be instituted in a District Commission within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the complainant resides or personally works for gain.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: File complaint in the District Commission where the consumer currently resides, without traveling to seller's location.

text:
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
Chapter IV: Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Section 35: Manner in which complaint shall be made

Statutory Text:
A complaint, in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided, may be filed with a District Commission by: (a) the consumer to whom such goods are sold or delivered or service provided; (b) any recognized consumer association; (c) central authority. The complaint may also be filed electronically (e-Daakhil). Every complaint shall be accompanied by such fee as may be specified.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Submit consumer complaint online via e-Daakhil without physical presence.

text:
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
Chapter IV: Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Section 38: Procedure on admission of complaint

Statutory Text:
The District Commission shall refer a copy of the admitted complaint within twenty-one days to the opposite party directing him to give his version of the case within a period of thirty days or such extended period not exceeding fifteen days. Where the complaint alleges a defect in goods which cannot be determined without proper analysis or test, sample shall be sent to an appropriate laboratory.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Opposite party must respond within 30 days of notice.

text:
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
Chapter IV: Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Section 39: Findings of District Commission and Reliefs

Statutory Text:
Where the District Commission is satisfied that the goods or services suffer from any of the defects or deficiencies specified in the complaint, it shall issue an order to the opposite party directing him to: (a) remove the defect; (b) replace goods with new goods of similar description; (c) return to complainant the price/charges paid along with interest; (d) pay compensation to consumer for loss or injury suffered due to negligence or mental harassment; (e) pay punitive damages; (f) cease and desist unfair trade practices.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Orders full refund with interest, mental harassment compensation, and litigation costs.

text:
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
Chapter IV: Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Section 69: Limitation period for filing consumer complaint

Statutory Text:
The District Commission, State Commission or National Commission shall not admit a complaint unless it is filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen. A complaint may be entertained after period of two years if complainant satisfies the Commission that he had sufficient cause for not filing within such period.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Consumer complaint must be filed within 2 years from date of deficiency/defect.

text:
Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020
General Rules: Duties of E-Commerce Entities and Marketplace Sellers
Rule 4: Mandatory Grievance Officer and Nodal Officer for E-Commerce Platforms

Statutory Text:
Every e-commerce entity shall appoint a Grievance Officer for consumer grievance redressal and display his name, designation and contact details prominently on its platform. The Grievance Officer shall acknowledge receipt of any consumer complaint within forty-eight hours and redress the complaint within one month from date of receipt.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: E-commerce platform must acknowledge complaint within 48 hours and resolve within 30 days.

text:
Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020
General Rules: Duties of E-Commerce Entities and Marketplace Sellers
Rule 5: Liabilities of Marketplace and Inventory E-Commerce Entities

Statutory Text:
No e-commerce entity shall adopt any unfair trade practice, whether in the course of business on its platform or otherwise. Every e-commerce entity shall effect all refunds within a reasonable period of time or as prescribed by the Reserve Bank of India or any other competent authority.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Platforms cannot deny refunds for defective, counterfeit, or misdescribed products.

text:
The Information Technology Act, 2000
Chapter IX & XI: Penalties, Compensation and Offences
Section 43A: Compensation for failure to protect sensitive personal data

Statutory Text:
Where a body corporate, possessing, dealing or handling any sensitive personal data or information in a computer resource which it owns, controls or operates, is negligent in implementing and maintaining reasonable security practices and procedures and thereby causes wrongful loss or wrongful gain to any person, such body corporate shall be liable to pay damages by way of compensation to the person so affected.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Claim financial damages against companies or financial institutions failing to protect personal data.

Chapter IX & XI: Penalties, Compensation and Offences
Section 66C: Punishment for identity theft

Statutory Text:
Whoever, fraudulently or dishonestly make use of the electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature of any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to one lakh rupees.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine for stealing passwords, OTPs, or biometric identification.

text:
The Payment of Wages Act, 1936
Chapter II: Payment of Wages and Deductions from Wages
Section 5: Time of payment of wages and settlement on termination / resignation

Statutory Text:
The wages of every person employed upon or in any railway, factory or industrial or other establishment shall be paid before the expiry of the seventh day after the last day of the wage-period where less than 1000 persons are employed, and before the tenth day where 1000 or more persons are employed. Where the employment of any person is terminated or resigned by or on behalf of the employee or employer, the wages earned and all final settlement dues shall be paid before the expiry of the second working day from the day on which employment ceased.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Full and final settlement and unpaid wages must be paid within 2 working days of resignation or termination.

text:
The Payment of Wages Act, 1936
Chapter II: Payment of Wages and Deductions from Wages
Section 15: Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment of wages

Statutory Text:
Where contrary to the provisions of this Act any deduction has been made from the wages of an employed person, or any payment of wages has been delayed, such person himself, or any legal practitioner or registered trade union, may apply to the Authority appointed by the State Government for a direction under sub-section (3). The Authority may direct the refund of the deduction or the payment of the delayed wages, together with such compensation as the Authority may think fit, not exceeding ten times the amount deducted or up to three thousand rupees in case of delayed wages.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: File an application under Section 15 before the Labour Authority within 12 months for wage recovery plus compensation.

text:
The Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
Chapter V-A: Lay-off and Retrenchment
Section 2A: Dismissal of an individual workman to be deemed an industrial dispute

Statutory Text:
Where any employer discharges, dismisses, retrenches or otherwise terminates the services of an individual workman, any dispute or difference between that workman and his employer connected with such discharge, dismissal, retrenchment or termination shall be deemed to be an industrial dispute notwithstanding that no other workman or union is a party to the dispute. The workman may make an application directly to the Labour Court or Industrial Tribunal after 45 days from approaching Conciliation Officer.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Approach Conciliation Officer or directly apply to Labour Court for reinstatement and back-wages.

The workman may make an application directly to the Labour Court or Industrial Tribunal after 45 days from approaching Conciliation Officer.

text:
The Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
Chapter V-A: Lay-off and Retrenchment
Section 25F: Conditions precedent to retrenchment of workmen

Statutory Text:
No workman employed in any industry who has been in continuous service for not less than one year under an employer shall be retrenched by that employer until: (a) the workman has been given one month's notice in writing indicating the reasons for retrenchment and the period of notice has expired, or the workman has been paid in lieu of such notice, wages for the period of the notice; (b) the workman has been paid, at the time of retrenchment, compensation which shall be equivalent to fifteen days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service or any part thereof in excess of six months; and (c) notice in the prescribed manner is served on the appropriate Government.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Retrenchment without 1 month notice pay and 15 days/year severance compensation is void ab initio.

text:
The Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
Chapter V-A: Lay-off and Retrenchment
Section 33C: Recovery of money due from an employer

Statutory Text:
Where any money is due to a workman from an employer under a settlement or an award or under the provisions of Chapter VA or Chapter VB, the workman himself or any other person authorized by him in writing may make an application to the appropriate Government for the recovery of the money due to him, and if the appropriate Government is satisfied that any money is so due, it shall issue a certificate for that amount to the Collector, who shall proceed to recover the same in the same manner as an arrear of land revenue.

text:
Maternity Benefit Act, 1961
Chapter I: Maternity Rights and Protections
Section 5: Right to payment of maternity benefit

Statutory Text:
Every woman shall be entitled to, and her employer shall be liable for, the payment of maternity benefit at the rate of the average daily wage for the period of her actual absence, including the period immediately preceding the day of her delivery and the period immediately following that day. The maximum period for which any woman shall be entitled to maternity benefit shall be twenty-six weeks.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Entitled to 26 weeks fully paid maternity leave if worked for 80 days in past 12 months.

Chapter I: Maternity Rights and Protections
Section 12: Dismissal during absence of pregnancy

Statutory Text:
When a woman absents herself from work in accordance with the provisions of this Act, it shall be unlawful for her employer to discharge or dismiss her during or on account of such absence, or to give notice of discharge or dismissal on such a day that the notice will expire during such absence, or to vary to her disadvantage any of the conditions of her service.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Termination during maternity leave is illegal; employer liable for prosecution and payment of full benefits.

text:
Model Tenancy Act, 2021
Chapter II: Tenancy Agreement and Security Deposit
Section 10: Security Deposit limits and refund timeline

Statutory Text:
The security deposit to be paid by the tenant in advance shall: (a) not exceed two months' rent, in case of residential premises; and (b) not exceed six months' rent, in case of non-residential premises. The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant on vacating the premises after making lawful deduction of liability with proper accounting.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Landlord cannot demand more than 2 months rent as security deposit and must refund it on handover.

text:
Model Tenancy Act, 2021
Chapter II: Tenancy Agreement and Security Deposit
Section 14: Prohibition of cutting off or withholding essential services

Statutory Text:
No landlord or property manager shall, either by himself or through any person, cut off or withhold any essential supply or service in the premises occupied by the tenant. Essential services include supply of water, electricity, passages, staircase light, conservancy and sanitary services. On application by tenant, Rent Authority may pass immediate interim order restoring supply and impose penalty on landlord.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Immediate restoration of electricity/water and financial penalty against landlord for illegal disconnection.

text:
Model Tenancy Act, 2021
Chapter II: Tenancy Agreement and Security Deposit
Section 21: Protection against arbitrary eviction and procedure for repossession

Statutory Text:
No landlord shall evict any tenant during the subsistence of tenancy agreement except by filing an application before the Rent Court on specified grounds: (a) tenant refuses to pay agreed rent for two consecutive months; (b) tenant has parted with possession without consent; (c) misuse of premises causing public nuisance; (d) structural alteration without consent. A landlord cannot forcibly lock out a tenant without a decree from the Rent Court.

Legal Remedy / Actionable Recourse: Landlord cannot forcibly evict or throw out belongings without a court decree.

Chapter V: Leases of Immovable Property
Section 106: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract and statutory notice to quit

Statutory Text:
In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for agricultural or manufacturing purposes shall be deemed to be a lease from year to year, terminable by six months' notice; and a lease of immovable property for any other purpose shall be deemed to be a lease from month to month, terminable, on the part of either lessor or lessee, by fifteen days' notice in writing.

text:
Government Dispute Redressal Mechanism: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP) & 1930 Helpline
Authority: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs
Helpline: 1930 (Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Helpline) | Portal: https://cybercrime.gov.in

Procedure & Mechanism:
National portal for immediate reporting of cyber financial frauds and cyber crimes against women/children. Dialing 1930 within the 'Golden Hour' (first 2-4 hours) triggers immediate lien / freeze on fraudulent beneficiary bank accounts through the Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System (CFCFRMS).
Actionable Remedy: Call 1930 immediately with transaction UTR/reference number to freeze stolen money before withdrawal.

Government Dispute Redressal Mechanism: Rent Authority / Rent Court
Authority: State Urban Development & Revenue Department
Helpline: None | Portal: https://delhi.gov.in/rent-authority

Procedure & Mechanism:
Statutory quasi-judicial authority established for expeditious adjudication of tenancy disputes, unreturned security deposits, and illegal eviction without long civil court delays.
Actionable Remedy: File a direct petition before the Rent Authority for recovery of security deposit with 18% per annum interest.
